## Japan Week at a Glance

For 2 adults, this route fits your dates, pace, and budget well: **Tokyo (3 nights) → Kyoto (2 nights) → Osaka (2 nights, with one nature/cultural day)**. It balances neighborhoods, temples, food, and one lighter scenic day without rushing.

## 7-Day Japan Itinerary

Day 1: Tokyo Arrival, Asakusa, and Sumida Riverside
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Tokyo, airport transfer, hotel check-in, and a slow start.
- Afternoon: Explore **Senso-ji Temple**, Nakamise shopping street for snacks, and nearby Asakusa lanes.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/19/20181123_Sens%C5%8D-ji-7.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Explore **Senso-ji Temple**, Nakamise shopping street for snacks, and nearby Asakusa lanes, Japan
- Dinner: Tempura, soba, or donburi in Asakusa; keep it easy after the flight.
- Stay: **Tokyo, Asakusa or Ueno** for good transit and a calmer atmosphere.
Action: [Button: Asakusa Guide] https://www.gotokyo.org/en/destinations/eastern-tokyo/asakusa/index.html

Day 2: Ueno, Yanaka, and Traditional Tokyo
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Visit **Ueno Park** and choose one museum or just enjoy the park and shrine areas.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d7/April_2009%2C_hanami_in_Ueno_Park_-23394.jpeg Alt=Morning: Visit **Ueno Park** and choose one museum or just enjoy the park and shrine areas, Japan
- Afternoon: Walk through **Yanaka**, one of Tokyo’s old neighborhood areas, with local shops and a slower pace.
- Dinner: Casual izakaya-style set meal or ramen in Ueno/Yanaka.
- Best for: Traditional streets, everyday Tokyo, and temple/neighborhood balance.
Action: [Button: Ueno Info] https://www.gotokyo.org/en/destinations/northern-tokyo/ueno/index.html

Day 3: Meiji Shrine, Omotesando, and Shibuya Backstreets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Meiji Jingu Shrine** and the surrounding forested grounds.
- Afternoon: Walk Omotesando and quieter parts of **Shibuya** for cafés, design streets, and people-watching without focusing on nightlife.
- Dinner: Sushi train, curry rice, or a teishoku set in Shibuya/Harajuku.
- Stay: Final Tokyo night before moving west.
Action: [Button: Meiji Jingu] https://www.meijijingu.or.jp/en/

Day 4: Tokyo to Kyoto, Higashiyama Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Take the **Tokaido Shinkansen** from Tokyo to Kyoto; drop bags at hotel.
- Afternoon: Explore **Higashiyama**, including **Kiyomizu-dera** approach streets, Sannenzaka, and Ninenzaka.
- Dinner: Kyoto-style set meal, tofu cuisine, or small kaiseki-style course at moderate budget.
- Stay: **Kyoto, Gion/Shijo/Kawaramachi area** for walkability.
Action: [Button: Kyoto Travel] https://kyoto.travel/en/

Day 5: Arashiyama and Western Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head early to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove**, then **Tenryu-ji Temple**.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/6e/Durchgang_im_Tenry%C5%AB-ji_Garten.jpg Alt=Morning: Head early to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove**, then **Tenryu-ji Temple**, Japan
- Afternoon: Cross **Togetsukyo Bridge**, riverside stroll, and optional monkey park only if energy allows.
- Dinner: Noodles, yudofu, or Kyoto curry near central Kyoto.
- Best for: Your **nature day**, with light walking and scenic views rather than a strenuous hike.
Action: [Button: Arashiyama Info] https://kyoto.travel/en/destinations/arashiyama/

Day 6: Fushimi Inari and Osaka Neighborhoods
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Early visit to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** to avoid crowds; do a partial hike instead of the full summit for a medium pace.
- Afternoon: Travel to **Osaka** and check in; explore **Nakanoshima**, **Utsubo Park**, or **Shinsekai by daylight** rather than nightlife-heavy districts.
- Dinner: Osaka classics such as okonomiyaki or kushikatsu in a casual restaurant.
- Stay: **Osaka, Umeda or Namba**, choosing a quieter side street hotel.
Action: [Button: Osaka Travel] https://osaka-info.jp/en/

Day 7: Osaka Castle Area, Kuromon or Dotonbori by Day, Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg
- Morning: Visit **Osaka Castle Park** or **Shitenno-ji Temple** depending on departure timing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ec/Osaka-jo_Castle_Evening_2024-07.jpg Alt=Morning: Visit **Osaka Castle Park** or **Shitenno-ji Temple** depending on departure timing, Japan
- Afternoon: Early food-focused walk at **Kuromon Market** or a daytime stroll around **Dotonbori** before heading to the airport.
- Dinner: If you have time before departure, keep it simple near Namba/Umeda or at the airport.
- Departure: Leave from **Osaka (KIX or ITM depending on your ticket)**.
Action: [Button: Kansai Airports] https://www.kansai-airport.or.jp/en/

## Budget Breakdown for Two

| Category | Estimated Cost (USD) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotels (6 nights) | 1,080 | Private ensuite rooms, mid-range business/boutique hotels at ~$160–$190/night |
| Intercity transport | 260 | Tokyo→Kyoto Shinkansen + Kyoto→Osaka local/regional train |
| Local transport | 180 | IC card use for subways, JR/local trains, airport transfers allowance |
| Food | 900 | About $60–$75 per couple for lunch + $70–$85 for dinner + snacks on some days |
| Temple/museum/sight admissions | 140 | Mostly low-cost; many shrines are free |
| Miscellaneous/café/snacks | 180 | Extra drinks, desserts, lockers, small purchases |
| Buffer | 460 | Price variation, airport transfer differences, nicer meal or taxi if needed |

**Estimated total:** **USD 3,200**
This is realistic if you book hotels early and keep most meals in the **casual to mid-range** band rather than splurge dining.

## Hotels and Transport Strategy

### Best stay pattern
- **Tokyo: 3 nights**
  - Areas: **Asakusa, Ueno, or Ginza East**
  - Target: **$150–$190/night** for a private double/twin room with private bathroom
- **Kyoto: 2 nights**
  - Areas: **Gion, Shijo, Kawaramachi, or Kyoto Station**
  - Target: **$160–$210/night**
- **Osaka: 1–2 nights**
  - Areas: **Umeda** for transit convenience or **Namba** for food access
  - Target: **$140–$180/night**

### Intercity transport suggestions
- **Tokyo → Kyoto:** Tokaido Shinkansen **Nozomi** is the fastest and easiest.
- **Kyoto → Osaka:** JR Special Rapid or local rail; cheap and simple.
- **Airport departure from Osaka:** Allow extra transit time if flying from **Kansai International Airport (KIX)**.

### Pass advice
- For this itinerary, a **nationwide JR Pass is usually not cost-effective**.
- Better option:
  - Use an **IC card** for city transport
  - Buy **individual Shinkansen tickets** for Tokyo→Kyoto
  - Use regular JR/private rail for Kyoto↔Osaka

## Practical Travel Notes

### 5 useful Japan tips
- **Carry some cash:** Cards are widely accepted in cities, but small temples, older eateries, and some local shops may still prefer cash.
- **Tipping is not expected:** In Japan, standard service is built in; leaving tips can feel awkward.
- **Pack light layers:** Mid-April is mild, but mornings/evenings can be cool; bring a light jacket and comfortable walking shoes.
- **Use luggage forwarding if needed:** If you dislike moving bags between cities, hotel-to-hotel forwarding can make the Tokyo→Kyoto move much easier.
- **Bring a small trash pouch:** Public trash bins can be limited, so carrying a small bag for wrappers/tissues is surprisingly handy.

## Quick Booking Priorities

- Book **hotels first**, especially in Kyoto, since spring demand can be high.
- Reserve the **Tokyo→Kyoto Shinkansen** once your arrival plans are firm.
- Keep dinners flexible except for **one Kyoto dinner** if you want a nicer traditional meal.

## Sources

- Japan National Tourism Organization: <https://www.japan.travel/en/>
- Go Tokyo official travel guide: <https://www.gotokyo.org/en/>
- Kyoto City Tourism Association: <https://kyoto.travel/en/>
- Osaka Official Travel Guide: <https://osaka-info.jp/en/>
- JR Central Tokaido Shinkansen: <https://global.jr-central.co.jp/en/>
